thread:
sam: heads up — saw a repro where rotating REDWOOD_API_KEY in the env didn't actually change which key an async client used for subsequent requests.

olga: ugh. reproduction steps?

sam: minimal case: create two AsyncClient instances in the same process, swap os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] and then call client.generate() from both. first client uses old key, second uses new key as expected, but after rotation some requests still go out with previous key randomly.

mike: that sounds like a session/transport-level cache. are we reusing an HTTP session per process?

sam: yes — AsyncClient keeps an aiohttp.ClientSession globally to reuse connections. the bug seems to be that the auth header is set at session creation and not refreshed when client-level api_key var changes.

ana (typo, corrected): @ana — can you check header behavior?

ana: sorry meant ana.

ana: (reacts :facepalm:)

ana -> ana: can confirm similar locally, but my setup used explicit API key passed into the client constructor, not env. when rotating keys we expected new Client(api_key=K2) to use K2 exclusively, but traces show K1 still used for a few requests.

ana: repro snippet i used:

```python
# simplified
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio

async def main():
    c1 = AsyncClient(api_key="K1")
    c2 = AsyncClient(api_key="K2")

    # schedule interleaved requests
    await asyncio.gather(c1.generate("hello"), c2.generate("hi"))

asyncio.run(main())
```

olga: hmm, looks like client instances share an internal auth middleware that captures header at first session init. iirc the runtime attaches headers onto the session connector.

mike: prioritization note: we intended env var fallback -> constructor arg -> rotation provider. but implementation probably memoized headers keyed only by session id.

sam: possible mitigations: 1) make session stateless wrt auth (set Authorization per-request), 2) scope sessions to client instance (avoid global session reuse), or 3) expose a `refresh_auth()` method on AsyncClient to rebind headers.

ana: from a DX standpoint, option 1 is best for predictability but might hurt perf. option 2 increases connections.

ana: also typing/pyright folks will want the async client to explicitly show how to pass a per-request auth callback. feature request: support an async api_key_provider callback that is invoked for each request, e.g. `api_key=AsyncKeyProvider.get` so rotation works without re-creating clients.

ana: example API proposal:

```python
# accept either str or Callable[[], Awaitable[str]]
client = AsyncClient(api_key=lambda: await my_kms.fetch_current())
await client.generate("x")  # client should call provider each request
```

olga: +1 on provider callback. we should also document precedence: explicit arg overrides env, provider overrides static string.

mike: i'll open an issue tracking three things: reproduce + minimal failing test, short-term doc warning about env rotation for long-lived processes, and an API design RFC for `api_key_provider`.

sam: thanks. FYI the intermittent nature makes it tricky to catch in unit tests; i'll attach network traces when i post the repro.

devex-bot: created issue DE-1423 for "AsyncClient auth headers not refreshed on key rotation" — https://redwood.internal/DE-1423

olga: nice. can we also add an example to quickstart showing recommended pattern for multi-client setups (explicit per-client keys or provider)? onboarding tickets keep showing users setting REDWOOD_API_KEY at process start then expecting rotation.

ana: agreed. small doc tweak avoids a lot of support noise.

mike: assigned DE-1423 to eng-runtime, tagging devex for docs. i'll add a test plan: 1) ensure new client with new key never sends old key, 2) ensure provider-based client fetches latest key for each request, 3) check perf impact of per-request header vs session-level header.

sam: if someone wants the repro i pushed a gist with a docker-compose + async script. link: https://gist.github.com/sam/repro-rotations

olga: thanks — grabbing it now.

ana: leaving a reminder to consider typing: allow Union[str, Callable[[], Awaitable[str]]] in stubs and docs + examples for sync vs async providers. pyright catches it but users get confused.

sam: yep — let's include a typed example in the SDK README.

mike: cool. wrapping up here, will follow up in the issue with a proposed code change. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: issue DE-1423 updated: PR draft opened by @mike 
"fix(auth): per-request auth provider for AsyncClient"

sam: awesome. thanks all!
